source.title: Puro-2B: Poor Lab's Qwen2-1.5B Trained on RTX 5090 within $5090
source.authors: Kairong Luo; Jiarui Cui; Yaorui Yin; Shengqi Chen; Yiming Yang; Linxiang Gao; Yanmohan Wang; Chengxia Li; Mingzhe Zhang; Kaifeng Lyu; Wenguang Chen

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. No apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extracting the relevant results.
record.tranche_reason: It uses scaling-ladder experiments and fitted relationships to examine validation loss across compute and downstream benchmark performance across training budgets; it is not a reproduction of the original scaling-law experiments.
record.gate_note: Relevant results are the matched validation-loss scaling ladder for optimizer and precision comparisons, and the fixed-2B Puro Cost Scaling Law based on downstream benchmark averages. Cross-model cost comparisons and SFT comparisons are not rows here: they do not test the named loss-scaling or budget-scaling relationships.
record.test_reason: The fixed-2B UD scale-down series reports a 15-benchmark average at five Phase 2 token budgets (51.98 to 56.00) and fits it against cost (RMSE 0.209). This is a result on whether downstream performance improves predictably with training scale (V6). The validation-loss ladder uses a shared-floor, shared-exponent power law only as a tool to estimate relative compute multipliers for MuonH and FP8. It reports no per-size losses or goodness of fit, so it does not test V1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Puro Cost Scaling Law is called a recipe-specific, fixed-2B scale-down relationship, not a universal law. The ladder fits are described as relative efficiency estimates, not absolute predictions. Note that the abstract attributes the $4.4K Qwen2-1.5B crossing to the fitted law, while Section 4.3.1 says the observed UD checkpoint itself exceeds Qwen2-1.5B. The authors also extrapolate the UD fit to assign CD and CMA endpoints cost-equivalents of ~$11.4K and ~$16.6K, beyond the observed range.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a fixed-TPP five-model ladder for relative optimizer and precision comparisons, plus a fixed-2B downstream performance-versus-cost fit; it does not reproduce the original broad loss-scaling or compute-optimal allocation experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: For the Puro cost-performance relation, fixing the Phase 1 cost at USD 1.84K and shifting the logarithmic fit reduced in-sample RMSE from 0.452 to 0.209. The optimizer comparison uses tuned, non-identical learning-rate schedules; leave-one-size-out results are reported for the fitted multipliers.

fits_no_version.finding: A Multi-Power Law (loss-curve law across LR schedules) is fitted to two anchor WSD schedules per peak at 0.6B. It predicts 15 unseen schedules with mean curve RMSE 0.0157 and endpoint MAE 0.0067. Using the effective LR instead of the scalar LR cuts held-out RMSE from 0.0265 to 0.0210 for 170M Muon runs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss curves under different learning-rate schedules are predictable from a few anchor runs via a schedule-dependent power-law model.

record.problems: The validation-loss ladder is limited to five model sizes and 20 tokens per parameter; its shared-shape fit is a relative comparison and does not report absolute large-run loss predictions. The downstream scaling curve holds architecture and recipe fixed, uses a 15-benchmark aggregate, and is explicitly recipe-specific. The paper reports fit RMSE and leave-one-size-out ranges but no statistical confidence intervals for these scaling results.
record.rows_left_out: Table 19 also reports the 15 individual benchmark scores for each UD budget, but the retained V6 rows record the aggregate measure used in the scaling fit. The paper's cost comparison across unrelated model families and its post-training results do not measure the claim versions catalogued here.

untested.parts: The power-law form is assumed in the ladder fit, not tested. No per-size losses, fit quality, or independent variation of N and D are reported. The ladder spans ~2 orders of compute (3.8e18–3.55e20) at fixed TPP=20.
Not tested. The authors say the ladder fit is not used to predict absolute 2B loss.
No compute-optimal allocation search. TPP=20 is taken from prior work.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
Text pretraining only. SFT results are not framed as scaling.
Only one model size (2B) and one recipe are used. The scaled variable is Phase 2 token budget only. There is no model-size scaling and no performance-versus-loss relation.
No test of how loss-law exponents or the compute-optimal split depend on fitting choices.

missing.what: Per-benchmark scores at each UD budget show non-monotone scaling for several tasks (GSM8K, HumanEval, BoolQ, MBPP). This bears on V6 at the individual-task level.
Per-size validation losses for the MuonH/Muon and FP8/BF16 ladders, needed to judge V1. They are only plotted.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V1 limits_scope label was dropped. It rested on parts of V1 that were not tested, which belong under untested. R1 and R2 also cannot show power-law behaviour. The reader's V6 limits_scope was likewise about untested generality; it is replaced with one based on per-task non-monotonicity and fit-shift dependence. Changed tranche from T2 to T3: downstream scaling at a fixed 2B model with cost as the scale variable is a new setting.

versions.untested_parts: Tests validation loss versus theoretical compute on a five-model ladder at a fixed 20 tokens per parameter, in matched optimizer and precision comparisons. Does not independently vary parameter count, tokens, and compute, establish scaling over several orders of magnitude, or report a general loss law across model families.
The paper says the ladder fit is not used to predict absolute loss for the 2B production run. It does not test whether small-run loss fits predict much larger runs.
No fixed-compute search for a loss-minimizing parameter/token split or growth exponents for compute-optimal parameters and tokens.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
The study concerns text pretraining and does not test other modalities, repeated-data regimes, fine-tuning, or transfer as scaling laws.

Tests the average of 15 downstream benchmark scores across UD Phase 2 training budgets for one fixed 2B model and recipe. Does not test whether individual downstream tasks generally scale across model families or as a function of pretraining loss.

The study compares shifted and unshifted fits for its recipe-specific downstream performance-versus-cost curve, but does not test how the original loss-law exponents or compute-optimal split vary with fitting choices, nor whether loss curves bend away from a single power law.

rows.subject: five-model ladder
rows.stage_stated: pretraining; 20 training tokens per scaling parameter
rows.operation_detail: Compared blockwise-FP8 MuonH with the updated blockwise-FP8 Muon baseline and fit validation loss against theoretical compute using a shared floor and exponent.

conditions.value: same data distribution, tokenizer, sequence length, batch size, and validation set

rows.measure: Validation loss versus theoretical compute; fitted compute-equivalent multiplier at matched loss
rows.value: 1.19× compute-equivalent multiplier for MuonH; 16.1% less theoretical compute at matched validation loss
rows.note: The reported result is an aggregate fit across the five-size ladder. It is a restricted shared-shape fit for a relative optimizer comparison, not an absolute loss prediction or a general test of the loss law.
rows.check: The value is a fitted MuonH-vs-Muon compute multiplier (1.19×) under an assumed shared power-law shape. It is a relative efficiency estimate and cannot show whether loss follows a power law. No per-size losses or fit residuals are given in the text. Marked 'partial' in the record; that state has no basis.

rows.subject: five-model ladder
rows.stage_stated: pretraining; 20 training tokens per scaling parameter
rows.operation_detail: Compared blockwise-FP8 MuonH with BF16 MuonH and fitted validation loss in theoretical-compute space.
rows.measure: Validation-loss gap and fitted BF16-equivalent compute retention
rows.value: Blockwise FP8 is 0.0031–0.0039 higher in validation loss across the five scales; fitted BF16-equivalent compute retention is 98.0%
rows.note: The text reports a cross-scale range rather than each scale's loss value. The fit estimates a precision-related horizontal shift, not the general power-law exponents.
rows.check: The value is an FP8-minus-BF16 loss gap and a fitted compute retention (98.0%). These are precision comparisons, not evidence on the power-law form. Marked 'partial' in the record; that state has no basis.

rows.subject: Puro-2B (UD scale-down series)
rows.operation_detail: Fitted average downstream benchmark performance against reproduction cost for UD Phase 2 runs, with Phase 1 cost held fixed.
rows.measure: Fitted downstream performance-versus-cost relationship and in-sample RMSE
rows.value: Shifted fit RMSE 0.209; the observed UD checkpoint at approximately $4.4K exceeds Qwen2-1.5B
rows.note: The authors call this a recipe-specific scale-down relationship, not a universal scaling law. The $4.4K comparison is supported by the observed UD checkpoint as well as the fitted trend.
rows.check: The fit is log-linear in incremental Phase 2 cost, with Phase 1 cost fixed at $1.84K as a shift. The 0.209 RMSE depends on that shift: the unshifted fit gives 0.452. This is in-sample only, over five points.

relationships.condition: Puro-2B UD Phase 2 budgets 60B–960B tokens, 15-benchmark unweighted average
relationships.reason: The average rises monotonically across the five budgets (51.98, 53.24, 54.01, 55.54, 56.00; R3–R7). A shifted log-cost fit gives in-sample RMSE 0.209 (R8).
relationships.display_finding: Average scores increased through 51.98, 53.24, 54.01, 55.54 and 56.00, with a shifted log-cost fit achieving an in-sample RMSE of 0.209.

relationships.condition: Individual benchmarks across the same UD budgets, and the choice of fit form
relationships.reason: From the text (Table 19), individual tasks are not monotone with budget: GSM8K drops 48.22→42.30 from 1/8 to 1/4, and HumanEval drops 25.00→20.73 from 1/8 to 1/2. Predictability holds for the aggregate, not per task. Fit quality also depends on the Phase 1 cost shift (RMSE 0.452 unshifted vs 0.209 shifted; R8).
relationships.display_finding: GSM8K fell from 48.22 to 42.30 between 1/8 and 1/4 budgets and HumanEval from 25.00 to 20.73 between 1/8 and 1/2, while shifting Phase 1 costs improved fit RMSE from 0.452 to 0.209.
